constraints: u * u + w * w == c * c
stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $B$, with $AB={=u}$ and $BC={=w}$. $D$ is the mid-point of $AB$ and $E$ is the mid-point of $BC$. Determine the length of $DE$.
solution: The triangle is right-angled at $B$, so by the theorem of Pythagoras $AC^{2}=AB^{2}+BC^{2}$.

$D$ is the mid-point of $AB$ and $E$ is the mid-point of $BC$, so $DE$ is the line joining the mid-points of two sides, and $AC$ is the third side. From the mid-point theorem we know: $AC=2\times DE$.
notes: Modelled on ex7-7-11c: Pythagoras gives the hypotenuse, then the mid-point theorem halves it (the segment joins the mid-points of the two legs). Legs come from a table of Pythagorean triples scaled by an even factor so the hypotenuse is even and DE is a whole number; hypotenuse capped at 60. That gives 20 distinct (AB, BC) pairs: 10 triples-and-factors, each with the legs in either order. The book's figure is replaced by a stem that states the right angle and both mid-points.
